title: UP RERA Kills Builder Extortion on Flat Transfers
excerpt: India's most populous state caps transfer fees at Rs 1,000 and opens an online complaint portal to stop builder overreach.
body:
Uttar Pradesh's real estate regulator just handed homebuyers a powerful weapon against one of the sector's most persistent rackets. Effective March 25, 2026, UP RERA's 10th Amendment caps flat transfer fees and arms aggrieved owners with a fast online complaint mechanism — ending years of unchecked builder profiteering.

**What changed — and why it matters:**
For decades, builders in UP charged transfer fees of Rs 200 to Rs 1,000 per square foot simply to update ownership records, pushing total bills as high as Rs 25–30 lakh in some documented cases. UP RERA Chairman Sanjay Bhoosreddy confirmed the authority had been flooded with such complaints. Under the new rules, a family transfer — such as inheritance by a spouse or child — can cost no more than Rs 1,000. A non-family resale transfer is now capped at Rs 25,000. Any demand above these limits is explicitly illegal under Regulation 47. Critically, a fresh sale deed or lease agreement is no longer required during the transfer process.

**The online complaint portal closes the enforcement gap:**
Knowing the fee caps exist is only half the battle — enforcement makes them real. If a builder demands more than the permitted amount, owners can now log a formal complaint directly on the UP-RERA portal at uprera.in, upload supporting documents, pay a nominal fee online, and track case status in real time. The system auto-assigns cases to the appropriate bench — Gautam Buddh Nagar for NCR projects, Lucknow for the rest — and generates notices to both parties electronically. The amendment also extends portal access to buyers of unregistered projects, a loophole builders had long exploited to escape scrutiny entirely.

**What to watch next:**
All eyes now turn to enforcement data — whether UP RERA publishes complaint resolution timelines and penalty orders that demonstrate the new rules have real bite.
